exposure: maternal attitudes toward EBF while living with HIV
conflicting information on EBF from biomedical, social, and personal sources
stigma associated with breastfeeding HIV-exposed infants
outcome: challenges to EBF uptake and adherence
cohort: The study included 27 purposively selected HIV-positive mothers with HIV-exposed infants younger than six months at a hospital in Eldoret, Kenya.
finding: Exclusive breastfeeding among HIV-positive mothers is influenced by a complex interplay of personal attitudes, social support, economic realities, stigma, and healthcare facility structures, alongside clinical factors like mode of delivery.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery was identified as a factor influencing breastfeeding initiation among HIV-positive mothers.
cross-section timing: Experiences of mothers with infants younger than six months
